articleBlocks: At first, this looked more like navigation terms than the real category.
Stern pushed me in that direction immediately.
Right kept that theory alive for a moment, but northeast still did not quite fit.
That was the moment the first idea stopped working.
Then Northeast made me stop thinking about navigation terms and start thinking about the real category.
Stern made sense as a toward the stern.
Right fit once I read it through the answer.
The answer was Words to indicate directions.
Up and Northeast then felt less surprising and more like the last pieces falling into place.
Looking back, the answer feels obvious in the best way.
solutionNarrative: I first read Stern and Right too literally and drifted toward navigation terms. Stern could be read as "toward the stern", while Right could be read as "right", so the board still felt open instead of solved.

Northeast changed the direction because "northeast" gave me a testable phrase, not just a loose topic. Once that line worked, I had a fixed place to put the repeated word and could go back through the earlier clues with a clearer target.

I then checked "toward the stern", "right", "forward", and "Up". Those checks mattered because each one landed as ordinary wording on its own, so I was not forcing five separate hints into one bag. The board started to behave like one phrase pattern across Stern, Right, Forward, Up, and Northeast.

That left very little room for the earlier false start. The answer was "Words to indicate directions", and the last step was simply making sure every clue used that same reading cleanly before treating the solve as finished.
